description.narrative:
This project is an anticipatory and early action drought response designed to address acute food insecurity and water scarcity in southern Galkayo, Somalia, where recurrent drought has pushed thousands of households into IPC Phase 3 and Phase 4 conditions. Following the national drought declaration in late 2025 and the poor performance of the Deyr rains, the intervention responds to escalating risks of hunger, livestock losses, displacement, and public health threats. Implemented jointly by Oxfam, SSWC, and CPD, the project targets the most drought-affected districts in South Mudug and prioritizes vulnerable groups including women, children, people with disabilities, elderly-headed households, and marginalized communities. Overall, the project will reach45,130 people across southern Galkayo.
Under the first objective of rapidly protecting household food security and basic needs, the project will deliver cash-based assistance to prevent further deterioration of food security and the adoption of harmfulcoping strategies. A total of 2,150 vulnerable households, equivalent to 12,900 people, will receive cash-for-food assistance for three months, with a transfer value of USD 80 per household per month using food secureity cluster MEB for Mudug. In addition, multi-purpose cash assistance will enable households to meet immediate food and essential needs during the peak of the drought, helping to stabilize consumption and preserve remaining livelihood assets.
The second objective focuses on ensuring accessto safe and sufficient water in drought-affected communities to reduce water-related public health risks. To achieve this, the project will rehabilitate six community boreholes located in Sadex Higlo, Duqaaqo, Saaxoqurun, Ceel-Akhwaan, Docol, and Laasacadale, restoring reliable access to safe water for households and livestock. This will be complemented by a Public Health Risk Assessment, which will inform targeted public health promotion, the development of IEC materials, and safe water chain messagingtoreduce the risk of waterborne diseases.
The third objective aims to strengthen protection and public health outcomes for populations facing heightened risks due to drought and displacement. The project will provide emergency cash assistance to 70 survivors of gender-based violence and individuals experiencing acute protection risks, enabling them to access immediate safety, health, and protection services. In parallel, the project will facilitate 12 community protection meetings with 60 participants each to identify and mitigate emerging protection risks, and conduct 12 lifesaving protection awareness sessions, including service mapping, reaching 120 participants per session to improve community awareness of available supportservices.
The projectwill further generate learning to strengthen anticipatory action programming. A cash impact assessment will be conducted to examine the effectiveness of anticipatory cash transfers, and a learning brief will be developed and shared with Start Ready partners to inform future drought preparedness and response initiatives.
The estimated lead time for this drought crisis is30 to 45 days, referring to the period between clear early warning signals and the point at which households begin irreversible coping actions such as distress migration, sale of productive assets, or withdrawal of children from school. Within this window, anticipatory actions are triggered and initiated early, with assistance then delivered over the planned project period to stabilisehouseholds and prevent further deterioration as drought impacts intensify in South Mudug.

participating-org.narrative: It is a Somali women non-governmental humanitarian organization at a national level founded in 1992 at Mogadishu - the capital city, by a group of Somali women intellectuals from cross-section of the community. The Save Somali Women and Children (SSWC) contributeto the creation of a safe and sustainable situation by supporting women to overcome marginalization, violence and poverty in their communities. It operates as a non-profit making organization that has the right to network with a variety of organizations that share similar values and vision. In Somalia women face a range of complex challenges that require multiple solutions. We work in the belief that women through their own efforts and in collaboration with local, national and international allies are central to transforming their own lives and the lives of their communities and population of which they are part. SSWC is women-led and women-centered organization (so its programs reflect the needs of those served) that have well functioning management, finance and programmatic structures and systems.
